blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Diplomatic disagreement in a British office is less about hiding your view than about making space for the other person to save face. You are still saying what you think — but you are saying it in a way that lets the other side move without losing standing.

The structure is simple: acknowledge first, then soften, then deliver. "I take your point about the timing — I can see that would make things easier. I'm just a little worried, though, that it might push us past the quarter. Would it be worth looking at a slightly later launch?"

Behind the politeness there is a firm position. The art is to arrive at it without ever making the other side feel corrected — which is the one thing that makes British colleagues close up for days.

items.q: According to the text, what is diplomatic disagreement mainly about?
options: Making space for the other person to save face
items.why: "less about hiding your view than about making space for the other person to save face."

items.q: What is the three-step structure the text describes?
items.why: "acknowledge first, then soften, then deliver."

items.q: In the example, what is the speaker's real, firm position?
options: A slightly later launch would be safer
The timing is perfect as it is
items.why: Sob a polidez, ele quer adiar: "Would it be worth looking at a slightly later launch?"

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Letting the other side keep their standing matters
How you say something affects how it is received
Being direct and telling someone they are wrong gets faster results
Politeness can carry a firm position underneath it
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo argumenta que fazer o outro se sentir corrigido é justamente o que trava a conversa.

items.q: The phrase "close up for days" suggests that being made to feel corrected…
options: damages the working relationship for a while
makes colleagues more open and talkative
has only a brief, minor effect
items.why: Inferência: "close up" (fechar-se) por dias indica um dano relacional que persiste, não algo trivial.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando o diretor antes da reunião com o CEO. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, so before you walk in there, let's be clear about what you actually want. You disagree with the launch date — you think it's too early — but the CEO is proud of that date. If you say it's wrong, he'll defend it, and then you're stuck.

So don't lead with the problem. Lead with his point. Something like: "I can absolutely see why an early launch is attractive — it gives us the first-mover advantage." That costs you nothing, and it tells him you're on his side.

Then soften, and use the conditional. Not "we can't hit that date" — try "I'm just a little concerned that it might stretch the team past the quarter." And then offer the alternative as a question, not an order: "Would it be worth looking at pushing it back two weeks?"

Notice you never told him he was wrong. You disagreed with the idea, not with the man. If you keep it that soft, he'll take it far more seriously than if you argue. Trust me on that one.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Sophie warn against saying the launch date is wrong?
options: The CEO will defend it and the director will be stuck
The date has already been announced publicly
items.why: "If you say it's wrong, he'll defend it, and then you're stuck."

items.q: What does Sophie tell the director to lead with?
options: The CEO's own point about the early launch
items.why: "Lead with his point… I can absolutely see why an early launch is attractive."

items.q: How should the alternative be offered, according to Sophie?
options: As a question, not an order
items.why: "offer the alternative as a question, not an order: 'Would it be worth looking at…'"

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "You disagreed with the idea, not with the man"?
options: You should only raise ideas, never problems
You should keep your real opinion secret
You can challenge the plan without attacking the person
You should let the CEO decide alone
items.why: Inferência: separar a crítica ao plano da crítica pessoal é o que preserva a relação.

items.q: What does Sophie imply about soft language in a disagreement?
options: It makes the point easier to ignore
It makes the point taken more seriously, not less
items.why: Inferência: "he'll take it far more seriously than if you argue" — quanto mais suave, mais peso.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "He rephrased his objection so the client could save face." To save face means to…
options: avoid embarrassment or loss of respect
items.why: Save face = salvar a face: evitar constrangimento ou perda de prestígio.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A blunt 'you're wrong' can damage a manager's ___ in front of the team."
items.why: Standing = posição / prestígio dentro do grupo.

items.q: "She always acknowledges the other view before raising her own." To acknowledge here means to…
items.why: Acknowledge = reconhecer o ponto do outro antes de discordar.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "He wanted to ___ the criticism, so he wrapped it in a compliment first."
items.why: To soften = suavizar: reduzir o impacto da crítica.

items.q: "When he feels corrected, he closes up for the rest of the meeting." To close up means to…
items.why: Close up = fechar-se, parar de se abrir e de participar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem numa discordância diplomática. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the early launch date." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Might it be worth looking at a two-week delay?" This phrase is used to…
options: gently propose an alternative worth considering
items.why: Worth looking at = vale a pena considerar; forma suave de propor uma alternativa firme.

items.q: "Let's hold off on the announcement until the numbers are clear." To hold off on means to…
options: delay or wait before doing something
items.why: Hold off on = adiar, esperar antes de fazer algo.

items.q: "She agreed in the room but never followed through." She…
options: failed to do what she had agreed
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui ela não o fez.

items.q: "I take your point, but I see it slightly differently." This is a way to…
items.why: "I see it slightly differently" é a forma britânica de discordar sem corrigir o outro.
